rows.question: What was the change in NAV during 2Q17 and what drove it?
rows.answer: In 2Q17, the portfolio NAV increased from $7,954.2M to $8,065.4M [PSERS 2Q17 Page 20 p.20], driven by contributions of $246.4M and a net value gain of $432.2M, partially offset by distributions of $567.4M [PSERS 2Q17 Page 20 p.20]. The top quarterly value drivers were Bridgepoint Europe IV (+$37.7M), New Mountain Partners III (+$34.6M), Baring Asia PE Fund IV (+$32.0M), CVC European Equity Partners V (+$30.4M), and Bridgepoint Europe III (+$22.9M), collectively contributing $157.6M [PSERS 2Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The largest detractor was Platinum Equity Capital Partners II, which depreciated by $34.6M [PSERS 2Q17 Page 21 p.21].
rows.judge_rationale: The agent's figures and drivers are all directly supported by the NAV bridge and net value driver pages, but several retrieved chunks (cash flow summary, vintage year diversification, performance summary tables) were not relevant to explaining the NAV change.

rows.question: What was the NAV change between 2Q17 and 3Q17 and the primary drivers?
rows.answer: The total portfolio net value change for 3Q17 (2Q17 to 3Q17) was +$243.5M, representing a 3.06% quarterly IRR [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The primary drivers of appreciation were Crestview Partners II (+$36.4M), CVC European Equity Partners V (+$22.9M), LLR Equity Partners IV (+$18.5M), Bain Capital Asia Fund III (+$16.4M), and Cinven Fifth Fund (+$14.9M), totaling +$109.1M [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The primary detractors were Platinum Equity Capital Partners II (-$11.5M), Cinven Sixth Fund (-$9.7M), Actis Emerging Markets 3 (-$5.3M), Psilos Group Partners III (-$4.8M), and Baring Asia Private Equity Fund III (-$4.0M), totaling -$35.3M; notably, Bridgepoint Europe IV and Apax Europe VII-B also showed negative performance solely due to a methodology change to reflect unrealized accrued carried interest [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21].

rows.question: Describe the valuation methodology applied to Level 3 investments in Q3 2025.
rows.answer: Level 3 equity investments ($7,030,763 thousand) are primarily valued using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) with WACC ranging 8.7%–31.1% (weighted average 17.0%) and exit multiples of 6.5x–24.0x (weighted average 16.3x), with a small portion valued via Transactional Value ($877 thousand) or Recent Round of Financing ($272,865 thousand) [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements]. Private debt investments ($846,537 thousand) use DCF with WACC of 8.3%–16.1% (weighted average 12.7%), while liquid debt investments ($2,311 thousand) use Third-Party Pricing [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements]. Investments in Affiliated Investee Funds ($81,668 thousand) are valued via DCF with WACC of 7.1%–24.6% (weighted average 14.7%) [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements]. More broadly, Level III fair value considers factors including acquisition price, nature of the investment, local market conditions, comparable company valuations, and current/projected operating performance [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements].

Investments at Fair Value and Investments in Affiliated or Unaffiliated Investee Funds
Investments at Fair Value
The Aggregator records public and private investments at trade date and closing date, respectively, and values its investments at fair value in accordance with ASC 820. Fair value is the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In the absence of observable market prices, the Aggregator’s investments are valued using valuation methodologies applied on a consistent basis as described below. Additional information regarding these investments is provided in Note 3. “Investments and Fair Value Measurement.”
The Aggregator’s determination of fair value is based on the best information available in the circumstances and incorporates the Aggregator’s own assumptions, including assumptions that the Aggregator believes market participants would use in valuing the investments, and involves a significant degree of judgment, taking into consideration a combination of internal and external factors, including appropriate risk adjustments for
non-performance
and liquidity.
